title: GLASS mocks, tomographic
summary: On 18 sampled GLASS mocks the mean χ²/dof of the seven joint B-mode tests against the analytic covariance lies between 1.00 and 1.09, more than 2σ above 1 for ξ− B (12–83′) and ξ± B (2–20′); the mock PTEs are consistent with uniform except for ξ± B (2–20′) (KS p < 0.05).
banner: GLASS mocks under a throwaway blind (mock-ensemble-tomo); the input cosmology is known
lacks: Sampled mocks have unit weights, Gaussian shape noise at the data's per-bin σ_e and n_eff, no PSF leakage and no additive B mode, so this run has no PSF section.
provenance: GLASS sampled mock on the v2 tomographic footprint, 18 seeds, nside 4096
nz_v2_bound9_full_tomo.txt, 4 bins, the same file as the blinded data run
generator sp_validation make_glass_sim.py @ 08b37ee0; measurement run/mock-ensemble-sampled @ c8f7b522, the estimators of the data run 7081c2d0
headline_note: KS p-value that the 18 mock PTEs of each joint B-mode test are uniform

tables.caption: Joint B-mode null tests over all ten bin pairs on 18 mocks, each against the analytic covariance. A PTE well below 0.05 means the mocks fail their own null test, or their PTEs are not uniform.
Mean mock χ²/dof is 1 when the analytic covariance describes the scatter of the mocks; about 0.9 mocks per test should have a PTE below 0.05 by chance.
